sec: Actions of GH versus IGF-1, BEAMS mnemonic and IGF-2

items.q: Match the hormone to its specific action on carbohydrate metabolism — 1) Growth hormone 2) IGF-1 … A) Diabetogenic (induces insulin resistance) B) Anti-diabetogenic (insulin-like action)
items.exp: On carbohydrates, GH is diabetogenic while IGF-1 is anti-diabetogenic. (Book p946)

items.q: Match the hormone to its action on lipid metabolism — 1) Growth hormone 2) IGF-1 … A) Lipolytic (increases circulating free fatty acids) B) Anti-lipolytic
items.exp: On lipids, GH is lipolytic increasing free fatty acids, whereas IGF-1 is anti-lipolytic. (Book p946)

items.q: What shared metabolic effects are exerted concordantly by both GH and IGF-1?
opts: Bone growth, epiphyseal growth, muscle anabolism, and protein anabolism
Adipose tissue lipolysis and ketone body formation
Hepatic glycogenolysis and systemic insulin resistance
items.exp: Both GH and IGF-1 stimulate bone growth, epiphyseal growth, muscle anabolism, and protein anabolism. (Book p946)

items.q: Under the BEAMS mnemonic for GH actions independent of IGF-1, which action is NOT included?
opts: Bile acid synthesis and cholesterol excretion
items.exp: BEAMS represents Bone growth, Epiphyseal growth, Adipose tissue lipolysis, Muscle anabolism, and Salt and water retention; bile acid synthesis is not included. (Book p946)

items.q: Why is IGF-1 referred to as a 'wonder molecule' in cellular physiology?
opts: Promotes genetic stability, stress resistance, and regulates telomere shortening
Completely suppresses oncogenic transformation across all cell types
Permits indefinite cellular replication without requirement of ATP
Serves as an irreversible suicide inhibitor of somatostatin receptors
items.exp: IGF-1 promotes genetic stability, stress resistance, and modulates telomere shortening. (Book p946)

items.q: Assess the feedback loop of IGF-1: I Circulating IGF-1 exerts negative feedback by inhibiting pituitary GH secretion. II IGF-1 stimulates hypothalamic somatostatin release.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: IGF-1 inhibits pituitary GH secretion and stimulates hypothalamic somatostatin release in a classic negative feedback loop. (Book p946)

items.q: A full-term infant with congenital isolated GH deficiency is delivered with normal birth length and weight. What explains normal intrauterine somatic growth in the absence of GH?
opts: Intrauterine growth and development is primarily dependent on IGF-2
Maternal GH crosses the placental syncytiotrophoblast in high concentrations
Placental lactogen independently activates adult somatotroph receptors
Thyroid hormone completely substitutes for GH in epiphyseal chondrocytes
items.exp: In GH deficiency, height at birth is normal because intrauterine growth depends on IGF-2 (Multiplication Stimulation Activity), which is not GH-dependent. (Book p946)

items.q: IGF-2 was historically designated in experimental physiology as Multiplication Stimulation Activity (___).
items.exp: IGF-2 is also called Multiplication Stimulation Activity (MSA). (Book p946)

items.q: Match the somatomedin to its primary tissue source and physiological regulator — 1) IGF-1 2) IGF-2 … A) Liver tissue; regulated by growth hormone B) Diverse tissues; regulation is not known / GH-independent
items.exp: IGF-1 is produced by liver tissue under GH regulation; IGF-2 is synthesized in diverse tissues and is independent of GH. (Book p946)

items.q: What cardiovascular action is exerted by IGF-1 on the systemic circulation?
items.exp: IGF-1 promotes cardiovascular development, cardioprotection, and vasodilation. (Book p946)

items.q: Which central nervous system effect is NOT attributed to IGF-1?
items.exp: IGF-1 promotes neural development, myelination, amyloid-beta clearance, and anti-inflammatory protection; it does not cause tau accumulation. (Book p946)

items.q: In the BEAMS mnemonic for GH actions, the letter 'S' stands for ___ and water retention.
items.exp: The 'S' in BEAMS denotes salt and water retention. (Book p946)
